guardrailNotes: Private Admin Review material only; this run cannot accept, publish, delete or directly modify canonical organization data.
Reactor design, maturity, funding, partnership and timeline claims remain separated from licensing, fueled operation, procurement, deployment and customer acceptance.

candidates.reviewerRationale: Coverage value: Canadian Strategic Missions Corporation's LEUNR capability and disclosed financing summary gain the historical 0.1 MWth basis, CSA TRL 4/5-to-6 maturity, and RD-029, ERA, NGen, Telesat and CNL records. Evidence: The 20 durable sources include Corporations Canada, CSA, National Defence, ERA, NGen, Telesat and the OECD Nuclear Energy Agency; they separate funded development from company goals. Mission/Public Need read: No new Mission or Public Need relationship is proposed; Arctic Domain Awareness and Edge Data Processing remain unchanged because the operating context shows representative unfuelled analogue and simulator activity, a planned manufacturing cell and remote-monitoring software, not a deployed power system. Unknowns: Two consecutive annual filings are overdue and a notice of intent to dissolve has been sent; licensing, qualified fuel, criticality, site and customer deployment also remain unresolved. Reviewer action: Verify the corporate warning, then compare the capability, disclosed financing summary, 25STDPX13, RD-029, ERA, NGen, Telesat and CNL operations before acceptance.
reviewWarnings: Corporations Canada lists CSMC as Active but flags two consecutive overdue annual filings and a notice of intent to dissolve; recheck immediately before any publication decision.
No reviewed public source establishes a CNSC vendor design review, licence application, approved site, environmental review, fueled criticality or operating reactor for CSMC or LEUNR.
CSA describes TRL 4/5 conceptual design moving toward TRL 6 detailed design; a company-stated July 2026 TRL 5 deadline has no public completion proof.
The NRC IRAP record defines an unfuelled instrumentation-and-controls prototype objective but publishes no completion or acceptance result.
OECD-NEA's 0.1 MWth, 130 C and fuel parameters are a 2025 historical design basis and require confirmation before buyer use.
No public CSMC agreement establishes qualified HALEU supply, fuel fabrication, reservation or delivery.
Telesat's arrangement is an MOU; pilots and commercial or operational arrangements require definitive agreements.
NGen funds manufacturing-process and factory-cell development, not a proven serial line or tens-to-hundreds annual production capacity.
ERA and the University of Alberta describe an unfuelled prototype or physical simulator, not a fueled reactor, criticality event or licensed facility.
Public contributions and total-project values have different bases and are deliberately not aggregated as financing or revenue.
The Canadian Explorers article is an attributed CEO interview, not independent proof of size, transportability, refuelling interval, output, manufacturing capacity, financing or deployment.
No named Indigenous community, northern utility, defence installation or site owner is publicly established as a LEUNR customer, consent partner or deployment host.
A peer-reviewed CNL-authored paper raises lunar heat-rejection limits for low-temperature light-water concepts but does not test LEUNR or establish terrestrial Arctic infeasibility.

organization.name: Canadian Strategic Missions Corporation
organization.description: Canadian Strategic Missions Corporation is a Waterloo-based Canadian space and defence technology company developing dual-use systems for strategic power, remote and Arctic operations, space resources, water purification and advanced sensing.

profile_data.portfolioScope: Development-stage micro-nuclear reactors; lunar water purification and resource processing; portable multi-sensor imaging; quantum-gravimetry sensing; and broader R&D in robotics, nanomaterials, electrochemistry, industrial automation and space systems.
profile_data.operatingModel: CSMC presents CSMC Nuclear as its wholly owned strategic-power subsidiary and CSMC Labs as its wholly owned R&D division for quantum, natural resources and other deep technologies.

organization.current_activity: On July 23, 2026, FedDev Ontario announced a $4.5 million contribution toward CSMC's $10.095 million micro-nuclear power development project for Arctic defence operations and remote energy applications.
organization.operating_context: Canadian Strategic Missions Corporation is a development-stage Canadian space and defence company. Its official portfolio includes wholly owned CSMC Nuclear and CSMC Labs, with work spanning portable micro-nuclear power, lunar-water processing, quantum sensing, robotics and related deep-technology research.
organization.canadian_footprint: FedDev Ontario identifies CSMC as Waterloo-based, while National Defence and federal registry records use a Toronto address. Public evidence does not establish a manufacturing or reactor facility at either location.

reviewed_questions.question: What CNSC pre-licensing, licensing and site pathway supports the company's stated 2029 LEUNR demonstration target?
reviewed_questions.context: CSMC states a 2029 demonstration target for its LEUNR concept, but the official organization page does not identify a target-specific CNSC pre-licensing, licensing or site pathway.

capabilities.name: LEUNR Micro-Nuclear Reactor
capabilities.summary: Develop a portable low-enriched-uranium microreactor derived from Canadian research-reactor technology to provide resilient power for remote, Arctic, defence and space applications; current work remains at funded prototype and demonstration-planning stage.

missionMatches.alignmentSummary: LEUNR's stated Arctic and remote-power posture could enable sustained operation of northern sensing and communications sites, although the reactor itself is an enabling power system rather than an awareness sensor.

after.publicSummary: CSA agreement 25STDPX13 provides C$1 million from 2025-07-31 through 2027-08-31 for representative unfuelled analogue testing intended to move LEUNR from TRL 4/5 conceptual design toward TRL 6 detailed design.

program.name: Emissions Reduction Alberta LEUNR Project
program.summary: An active C$10.4 million Edmonton project with C$5 million of ERA funding for CSMC and the University of Alberta to commission an unfuelled prototype and prepare requirements and design for a future fueled research reactor.

participation.publicSummary: ERA identifies CSMC as the technology developer and University of Alberta as project partner for an unfuelled LEUNR prototype and future research-reactor design package.

program.name: Automated Manufacturing for Nuclear Micro-Reactors
program.summary: A C$3 million project with a C$1.2 million public contribution to develop an in-factory LEUNR manufacturing cell, led by CSMC with Samuel Automation and Stern Laboratories.

participation.publicSummary: NGen identifies CSMC as lead and Samuel Automation and Stern Laboratories as partners; the project develops manufacturing capability and does not establish an operating serial-production line.

value.publicSummary: Telesat and CSMC signed an MOU to explore Lightspeed-supported monitoring, operation and sustainment of CSMC reactor systems in remote and Arctic settings. Potential pilots and commercial or operational arrangements remain subject to definitive agreements.

operations.reviewerExplanation: Add organization relationship with Canadian Nuclear Laboratories for the OECD-reported November 2024 SLOWPOKE-2 licensing term sheet, not a licence or regulatory approval.

value.publicSummary: OECD-NEA reports that CSMC signed a November 2024 licensing term sheet with Canadian Nuclear Laboratories to use SLOWPOKE-2 as LEUNR's technical basis. A term sheet is not a completed technology licence, CNSC approval, site authorization or operating reactor, and no CNL confirmation was located.

corroboration.claim: LEUNR maturity is bounded by the CSA TRL 4/5-to-6 record and the ERA or University of Alberta unfuelled-prototype descriptions.
The historical reactor design basis and unresolved licensing or fuel posture are independently recorded by OECD-NEA and checked against CNSC's current public VDR surface.
Remote-monitoring development is supported separately by NATO DIANA, the DND RD-029 record and Telesat's counterparty MOU.
The Canadian operating picture separates a Waterloo description, Toronto registered office and Edmonton project rather than collapsing them into one headquarters claim.

candidates.executiveRelevanceSummary: CSMC matters as a Canadian attempt to turn research-reactor heritage into portable power for remote, defence and lunar settings. Public records show multiple funded workstreams across conceptual and detailed design, unfuelled simulation, manufacturing-process development and secure remote monitoring. They do not yet establish a CNSC licence, qualified fuel supply, fueled criticality, deployment site, customer order or commercial power delivery. A first conversation should reconcile the corporate filing warning and the design, licensing, fuel and 2028-2030 milestone dependencies before treating LEUNR as deployable capability.
